events.notes:
Mountain Fishtail Palm — Caryota maxima
What this page is actually about: A giant, fast-growing Asian mountain palm with unmistakable fishtail leaves and a reproductive cycle that slowly works down the trunk and ends with the death of the entire palm.
page.at_a_glance
Current draft has four bullets: twice-divided fishtail leaves; monocarpic flowering; six feet of annual growth; and its huge Asian/elevational range.
I would keep the first two essentially intact. They are exactly what At a Glance should do.
— Caryota is the only palm genus with twice-divided leaves. The smaller leaf segments have ragged ends shaped like fish tails.
— This palm flowers only once. Over several years, enormous flower clusters appear progressively lower down the trunk; when the sequence reaches the bottom, the palm dies.
— Mountain Fishtail Palm can grow remarkably fast under good conditions and eventually tower over most other palms in the park.
I would cut the fourth bullet about the native range. “Eastern Himalayas through Southeast Asia to Java” is good information, but it isn't a hook when the next section exists specifically to tell me where it comes from.
I'm also uncomfortable with “six feet in a single good year — among the fastest growth rates of any palm.” The first part may be supportable; the comparative superlative needs verification. More importantly, exact six-foot growth doesn't need to be in At a Glance and How It Grows.
So: 3 bullets, not 4. That's enough.
